newsitem.title: USA: Hashimoto says to leave currency talk to finmins.
newsitem.headline: Hashimoto says to leave currency talk to finmins.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said Friday that he and President Clinton had touched on a discussion of currencies and would leave further talk on the matter to the finance ministers.

"As far as the exchange rate question is concerned we believe that having touched on this matter between ourselves, it is more proper to leave the matter to (U.S. Treasury) Secretary Rubin and (Japanese Finance) Minister Mitsuzuka," Hashimoto said at a news conference following talks with Clinton.

Rubin and Mitsuzuka will meet Sunday ahead of taking part in a meeting of Group of Seven finance ministers and central bankers, and Rubin said on Friday that he expected foreign exchange markets to be discussed.
Hashimoto also said he had reassured President Clinton that he was confident Japan would grow through domestic demand.
"I also communicated to the President that it is with confidence that we expect Japan's economy will grow with the strength of domestic demand," Hashimoto said.
The U.S. administration has repeatedly called on Japan to stimulate domestic demand and warned against a rise in its current account surplus.
